explanation: The theorem says that z ↦ (x − I·z)^n · exp(−π z²), as a complex-valued function on ℝ, is integrable. I found no Mathlib declaration for this. I checked the Gaussian integrability lemmas in Analysis/SpecialFunctions/Gaussian (GaussianIntegral.lean and FourierTransform.lean): `integrable_rpow_mul_exp_neg_mul_sq`, `integrable_cexp_neg_mul_sq`, `integrable_mul_cexp_neg_mul_sq`, `integrable_cexp_neg_mul_sq_add_real_mul_I` and the `integrable_cexp_neg_*_add` variants. Each covers a real power or a linear factor times a Gaussian, or a shifted complex Gaussian. None covers a complex polynomial factor (x − I z)^n. To get the result from them you would still need the same bound the library proves, ‖x − I z‖^n ≤ 2^n(|x|^n + |z|^n), plus a domination argument. That is more than one or two lines of glue. Name searches for pow/polynomial × gaussian/exp_neg integrability lemmas found nothing else relevant.
